  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Multinomial logistic regression is explicitly recommended as the appropriate categorical-response model for predicting 5-level Stim Paradigm from the five performance variables. This is superior to forcing ordinary linear regression because: (1) the response is strictly categorical with no natural ordering, (2) linear regression would violate distributional assumptions and produce nonsensical predictions outside valid category indices, (3) multinomial logit directly models class probabilities and provides interpretable log-odds coefficients for each paradigm versus a reference (e.g., Sham). Alternative: random forest or gradient boosting for non-linear relationships, with feature importance to identify which performance variables best discriminate paradigms. Given the large class imbalance (Combined=63.7% of data), use stratified sampling or class weights in model training and report balanced accuracy, macro-averaged F1, and per-class precision/recall.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [

    "Assess independence assumption: verify no repeated measures structure within Mouse (8 mice with 7233-10986 trials each); if present, use mixed-effects models with Mouse as random effect",

    "Examine influential observations given extreme max values (Time-to-Target max=201.39, Path Efficiency max=29.82)"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined paradigm will show highest Success rate (~0.78) and lowest Time-to-Target (~2.56s), significantly outperforming Sham (Success=0.27, Time-to-Target=4.68s) and unimodal conditions",
    "Sham will show worst performance on all metrics: lowest Success, highest Time-to-Target, lowest Path Efficiency, lowest Average Speed, and lowest AD",
    "ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only will perform intermediately and similarly to each other (Success ~0.67-0.69, Time-to-Target ~3.05-3.14s), with no significant difference between unimodal modalities",
    "Bright Visual Only will outperform Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only, approaching Combined performance (Success=0.78 vs 0.78), suggesting visual salience matters",
    "AD (angular dispersion) will be highest in Combined and Bright Visual Only (~0.39-0.40), intermediate in ICMS Only (~0.35), and lowest in Sham (~0.24), indicating more exploratory or directed movement patterns with effective stimulation",
    "Multinomial model will achieve highest classification accuracy for Combined (majority class) and Sham (most distinct), with confusion between ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe class imbalance: Combined comprises 63.7% of trials while Bright Visual Only and Sham are only 4.3% and 4.6% respectively, limiting power for comparisons involving rare classes and biasing predictive models",
    "Unclear whether trials are independent: 8 mice contribute 7233-10986 trials each, likely violating independence assumption; need mixed-effects or clustered standard errors",
    "Success is binary but treated as mean in summaries; need trial-level binary analysis",
    "Path Efficiency shows extreme right skew (max=29.82 vs mean=0.47) suggesting outliers or calculation artifacts",
    "No information about trial sequence, learning effects, or session structure that could confound paradigm comparisons",
    "Temperature=0.0 in metadata suggests deterministic LLM generation, but this is irrelevant to statistical analysis",
    "Single replication (Run ID 8, Replication 1) means no estimate of run-to-run variability for this analysis configuration"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a mixed-effects multinomial logistic regression with Mouse as random intercept, using the five performance variables to predict Stim Paradigm, with class weights to address imbalance. Finally, conduct mediation analysis to test whether Path Efficiency and AD explain the relationship between stimulation paradigm and Time-to-Target."
}
